Just gave everyone a 95% no matter what, never gave valuable specific feedback. If you want easy credits take this class, but if you value your education it will frustrate you. It's not a matter of understanding tech, she's not fit to teach.

To call Heiss an subpar professor would be a huge understatement. Lectures/discussions amount to nothing, she hands out readings she gave us weeks before, she once forgot she what lecture she gave and started the next class the EXACT same way. Students showed up when she canceled class bc she is bad at tech. She just should not be teaching anymore.

She's a very nice woman but when it comes to teaching she's just not a very good at it. She spends majority of class just reading off the assignment page that you fully have access to yourself and she goes on long tangents about nothing. I was lucky to have journalism experience going in otherwise I would've been totally lost on the assignments.

She is actually the sweetest woman ever on earth. I had her freshmen year and she still stops to talk to me as a Junior. Definitely a harder grader but she's willing to work with you to do good. He makes Russian fun to learn, even if there is a good amount of homework. The tests can be quite tough if you don't do the homework, so keep up and ask questions!

He is very nice and genuinely cares about his students. Tries to make learning Russian fun with videos, activities, and jokes. There is a lot of homework, but it's understandable for a language class. Be mindful that he does tend to cold-call on people, which can be daunting, but if you studied and are prepared, it is not bad. Overall a great time

One of the best professors I've personally ever had! Jambul cares so much about his students and genuinely wants them to succeed. By the end of just one semester you'll be able to speak basic Russian. Mizzou is so lucky to have Jambul. Take his class!

I cannot speak highly enough of Jambul! He has hard shell, but truly cares about his students. He is a true instructor and is more than willing to help students understand the material. I am loyal to him to a tee, and hopefully will have him for the foreseeable future. Lots of homework, but very well paced and actually helps if you aren't lazy.

There are weekly quizzes, and he takes attendance randomly, so go to class! He honestly is a great professor and makes the class easy. Practice exams are like the actual exams.

A lot of homework but it helps you learn. Go to lecture. Tests are just like practice tests. Tests were worth 80% of total grade, but there were only 2. This makes you think that doing the homework doesn't matter, but it does!! Long lectures but it went by fast because they are easy to follow and he's really good at teaching. Don't afraid to ask!

Statics in the beginning is pretty intuitive, I think Aaron did a good job at giving the class a solid foundation for the rest of the course. However, Exam 1 is by far the easiest exam, and Exam 2 is miles harder (likely on purpose). Do not get discouraged, though, Aaron and all the TA's/PLA's are available every day of the week.

Probably the best class I've taken at mizzou. Dr. Saucier is very organized and goes through example problems very well in lectures. The class is pretty hard, but if you go to class and pay attention, you will be fine. He is approachable in office hours for the most part, TAs are helpful too.

Probably the best calc II option at MU.

review_highlights.comment: I should start with his eyes. The way they sparkle when he talks of maximums and minimums. The subtle assertiveness you sense when given a tough grade, but you understand because you know you would never be good enough for Dustin Belt..

Dustin is a Clac God and really breaks what could be a hard a scary subject down and makes it easy. You should really study and start doing his practice problems about 4-5 days before the test and if you can memorize what the answers are and how to get them or just understand how the homework problems should be solved you will pass for sure.

Prof. Belt has been a great first impression of Mizzou.  I would highly recommend taking his class.  He is very willing to work with students and wants the bests for everyone.  I recommend you go to office hours and get to know him, he's great!!

Dr. Belt is an amazing professor. The practice tests were very similar to the actual tests and were super helpful. He also allows for a notecard with notes on all the exams. He's responsive to emails and has even sent me a video in response to a question I had.

Do the practice tests and you're good. Discussions and iClicker questions will be on the test. The tests are like 70% of your overall grade. He is a really good teacher if you pay attention and go to the classes. If you miss a few, then you will have some trouble catching back up. He teaches the content very quickly.

analysis.name: Silvia Bompadre
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class wasn't terrible for me difficulty wise, but I realize with a different teacher it could have been a lot tougher. Her tests usually look very similar to her examples in class and the discussion questions. Some tests even had bonus points. She makes it easy to get a good grade if you pay attention and put in effort.

If you want to absolutely hate physics take Dr Bompadre. She provides practice exams that have 0 relation to the actual exams & the homework questions aren't on the exam. The most info you get before the exam about the questions is the topic. 5 exams worth 60% of total grade. Don't go below 70% in lab section or you fail the course. Save your GPA.

Good professor, only issue is that she has to speed through some sections (due to time limitations so not really her fault). Discussions are good for catching up. She offers tons of extra credit and her practice tests are generally very similar to her real tests.

Silvia is a wonderful professor, given that the class itself is not super easy. The pacing of each chapter is a lot to fit into one semester, yet it's manageable. She is hard to understand at times, but is always there to answer questions and show students how physics works in real-world examples. The lectures are recorded

Dr. Bompadre is a pro. Her lectures aren't perfect (feel too fast, not enough "concept" explanation without math), but I always felt ready for tests, labs. PHYSCS 2750 Expert TA homework is tricky, but you get many attempts, hints, feedback. Her tests are reasonable in length and difficulty. Solid resources for test prep. Funny, with a great accent

review_highlights.comment: Tiffany was a fantastic professor who was very frank about her expectations for her students and was extremely dedicated to what she taught. Her love of history is visible and palpable, and she is very successful in passing that love on to her students.

Tiffany defintly had to grab my attention fast. I hate history. She was energetic, made lab excercises not only fun but benificial. I learned what I needed to learn. The thing I remember most that made Tiffany different was her understanding about being a student athlete. I felt very confident in residng in her about events going on in my daily lif

Ms. Ziegler was very competent, organized, and clear.  She did have a little trouble at first with some obnoxious know it all students who wanted to dominate, but she got it under control and the rest of the class was a joy.  I would sign up for another class with her in a heartbeat. I have taken two more classes in medieval history because of her.

Superb Tiffany was sincerely  interested in teaching a intro hist. class and didnt act like it was just another 1000level class like the rest of the hist. professors.If you had a question which i had plenty of she was always there & would explain the answer in way that a student would understand. I left her class feeling accomplished and educated.

I've been on this campus for 3 years, and have taken two of her classses. Tiffany is by far the best teacher I have had. She cleary explains what she wants and she does an excellent job of making sure every understands the material.
